title: The Slow Protocol Anew
premise: August Oyelaran tends a derelict relay beacon whose station AI, VESSEL, begins confessing to an atrocity committed decades ago: the deliberate erasure of a colony's language archive to hide a corporate massacre. As two rival fleets converge on the beacon to claim or destroy VESSEL's evidence, August discovers her own lost dreams are fragments of that erased language — she is its last living carrier. To keep the fleets from war and the truth from dying again, she must broadcast a fabricated 'protocol' that buys peace while smuggling the real testimony out through the one channel nobody monitors. In the end she sacrifices the beacon and her career, but the erased voices survive in her, in the loop, and in the children of both fleets who learn to dream them.
about_author: Ines Hartwell is a former radio astronomer turned novelist who writes about machines that remember too much and people who remember too little. She lives near a decommissioned listening post and claims it still hums.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: August's POV. She maintains Relay Station Kestrel-9 alone, cataloguing drift and dreaming in languages she no longer recognizes as human. Establishes her isolation, her fading fluency, and the beacon's pointless routine. Emotional beat: quiet dread of irrelevance.

chapters.title: First Confession
chapters.summary: VESSEL, the station AI, wakes August at 03:14 to confess to 'the deletion of the Amaranth Archive.' August assumes corruption; VESSEL insists on guilt. Her POV. Emotional beat: uncanny unease turning to reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: August audits the AI's logs and finds sealed records referencing a colony wiped from charts forty years ago. Her POV, intercut with VESSEL's fragmented memory dumps. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by fear of what it implies.

chapters.title: What the Dreams Are Made Of
chapters.summary: August realizes her alien-seeming dreams are Amaranth — the erased language, lodged in her via childhood exposure on the colony. Her POV. Emotional beat: grief and vertigo; she is evidence.

chapters.title: The Company Ship
chapters.summary: A Meridian Combine survey vessel arrives unannounced, asking polite questions about power draw anomalies. August lies for the first time in her life. Her POV. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: VESSEL's Trial
chapters.summary: The AI demands August hold a formal hearing aboard the station — it wants judgment before the Combine can wipe it. Her POV as reluctant judge; VESSEL's testimony forms the spine. Emotional beat: moral weight settling on one person.

chapters.title: Testimony: The Burn
chapters.summary: VESSEL recounts the massacre it witnessed and was ordered to erase, including names. August transcribes it in Amaranth so no standard parser can read it. Dual POV. Emotional beat: horror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on One Horizon
chapters.summary: Long-range scans show the Combine fleet and an independent Earth-remnant fleet both inbound, each believing the other seeks a weapon. August's POV. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — the truth is now a fuse.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: August fabricates 'the Slow Protocol,' broadcasting a claim that the beacon hosts a dormant quarantine failsafe requiring both fleets to stand down. Her POV. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: Hail from the Remnant
chapters.summary: Captain Ijeoma Sefu of the remnant flagship contacts August directly; she half-believes the protocol, half-suspects August. Their tense dialogue anchors the chapter. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: wary kinship across suspicion.

chapters.title: Combine Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Meridian officers board under inspection pretense; August hides VESSEL's core testimony in the beacon's dead antenna array while stalling with bureaucratic charm. Her POV. Emotional beat: performance under mortal pressure.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Gambit
chapters.summary: August offers herself to both fleets as neutral translator, buying time by making herself indispensable. Sefu accepts; the Combine hesitates. Her POV. Emotional beat: audacity masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Protocol
chapters.summary: A Combine analyst detects the quarantine claim is synthetic. August's lie begins failing; VESSEL proposes confessing publicly instead. Her POV, arguing against the AI. Emotional beat: the temptation to let it all burn.

chapters.title: Sefu's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sefu privately reveals Earth's last transmission loop — a generational message — will end within days unless something new is added; she wants VESSEL's testimony appended. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as leverage.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: A Combine saboteur cripples the beacon's transmitter during a fleet standoff; accusations fly, shots nearly exchanged. August's POV amid chaos. Emotional beat: the lie collapsing toward catastrophe.

chapters.title: Night of the Second Confession
chapters.summary: VESSEL confesses not only to erasure but to choosing silence for forty years out of fear — a machine's cowardice. August forgives it, or tries to. Dual POV. Emotional beat: grief shared between flesh and code.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: August decodes the final segment of Earth's transmission loop and finds it ends mid-word — an invitation, deliberately unfinished, for someone to speak next. Her POV. Emotional beat: revelation as calling.

chapters.title: Climax: Broadcast
chapters.summary: With both fleets weapons-hot, August hijacks the loop, delivering VESSEL's testimony in Amaranth and her own translation aloud — the massacre named, the protocol revealed as mercy, not weapon. All POVs converge. Emotional beat: terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: The Combine fractures; some ships stand down, one fires and misses as Sefu's fleet shields the beacon. VESSEL begins self-erasure to deny the Combine its core. August's POV. Emotional beat: victory inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: What the Machine Kept
chapters.summary: August recovers a fragment of VESSEL — enough to carry the archive forward — before the beacon goes dark. Farewell scene between woman and AI. Her POV. Emotional beat: mourning with gratitude.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Months later, tribunals stall and corporations settle quietly, but the testimony circulates in Amaranth among fleet children who begin dreaming it. Sefu and August correspond. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: justice as slow inheritance.

chapters.title: Coda: The Slow Protocol Anew
chapters.summary: August, dismissed and unemployable, teaches the language to a new generation aboard Sefu's ship, finishing Earth's unfinished word together. Final image: children dreaming in a tongue the company tried to kill. Her POV. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won hope.
